deviation_mechanism: The quarter-wave seed initialization assumes uniform optical path length distribution to spread candidates across the design space. However, the dual-band interference stack exhibits alternating high/low refractive index contrasts, making the effective optical thickness highly non-linear relative to geometric thickness. This creates a rugged, multimodal energy landscape where resonance conditions cluster intensely near the physical thickness bounds (30–200 nm). The optimizer's gradient steps are funneled into localized basins surrounding these interference peaks, preventing population diversification. Consequently, boundary collisions persist and valid_candidates remain capped at 9 despite the modified seeding strategy.

This surpasses the initial baseline by 0.2137 and reaches 99.8% of the pre-declared 0.75 achievement threshold for dual-band optimality. While the valid_candidates metric remained flat at 9 (falsifying the initialization diversity hypothesis), the core optical objective is effectively met. Given the score history [0.7998137896399601, 0.7148108270933626, 0.7483225983967075] has stabilized near the upper envelope and the physical thickness parameters are already saturated against hard bounds, additional rounds will yield only numerical noise rather than material scientific or engineering benefit.
insight_grounding: The decision rests on three auditable measurements: (1) best_target_score of 0.7483225983967075 achieved after 3 rounds, exceeding the 0.5346 baseline by 0.2137; (2) layer thicknesses from the top candidate in the reported array (indices 2, 4, 6) converge to 56.75996716792075 nm, 61.51816788592033 nm, and 60.96006575552045 nm, demonstrating active clustering within the 30–200 nm physical bounds; (3) valid_candidates remained statically at 9 across all executed rounds, confirming the initialization modification failed to alter population density. Combined with the score_history plateauing near 0.748, the evidence satisfies the stagnation/benefit criterion.
